homes.verdict: A 1963 fixer at $375k, 6.5 minutes from YWAM, with 5 bedrooms, a basement kitchenette, no HOA, and only $1,535 a year in tax — and the county values it $103k ABOVE the asking price. The catch is real though: it's sold as-is and the seller excluded FHA and VA financing, which usually means the condition wouldn't pass those appraisals. Worth touring, but bring a contractor, not just an inspector.

offer.rationale: 36 days on market with one cut already ($385k to $375k), and the seller is selling as-is. Push on price rather than repairs — an as-is investor listing that excluded FHA/VA won't have appetite for a repair addendum. Counterweight: 102 saves and investor demand mean a deep lowball probably won't land, so $350k is a real offer rather than a fishing expedition.

homes.verdict: Genuinely the nicest house we've seen — Wolf and Thermador kitchen, cherry cabinets, Pikes Peak views off a wraparound deck, 5 beds, finished basement, cul-de-sac corner lot backing open space, and only $40/mo HOA. The problem isn't the house, it's the risk stack and the price position: Rockrimmon is named in the videos as BOTH a wildfire-insurance hotspot AND one of the worst areas for expansive-soil foundation damage, the roof is listed only as "Other" on a 1978 build, and at $599,900 you'd have $100 left against your ceiling. Worth pursuing — but get the insurance quote and a structural engineer before you fall for the view.

wildfire.text: Rockrimmon is named in the videos as a wildfire-risk area where premiums run as high as $15,000 a year, and this lot backs to open space — exactly the exposure pattern insurers price hardest. Get a written quote for this address BEFORE you tour. It could add $300-900 a month.

soil.text: Rockrimmon is called out specifically as one of the worst areas for expansive-soil foundation damage — steep terrain, heavy clay, close to the mountains. On a 1978 house this needs a structural engineer, not just a general inspector. One Rockrimmon buyer was quoted more than double their budgeted insurance at underwriting because of shifting ground.

roof.text: The roof material is listed only as "Other" with no age stated, on a 47-year-old house. That's not an answer. It isn't Class 4, so there's no insurance discount — budget $11,000-25,000 and ask the seller for a Class 4 roof specifically.

plumbing.text: 1978 is the first year polybutylene supply pipe was used. It fails without warning and is often uninsurable. A clay or cast-iron sewer lateral is also likely at this age. Identify the pipe material and scope the sewer.

priced-high.text: The county values this at $580,069 and it's listed at $599,900 — about $20k above. It's already been cut $20,100 once and still hasn't sold in 27 days.

no-cushion.text: At $599,900 you'd have $100 of room against your $600k ceiling, on a 1978 house with an undisclosed roof. There's no reserve left for whatever the inspection turns up.

stucco.text: Stucco is listed in the exterior materials. Check it closely for hail pock marks and cracking — that's a known tell here.

flood-ok.text: Flood risk is clean: FEMA Zone X unshaded, minimal-risk. One of the two big pre-tour checks already passes.

financing-ok.text: Cash, conventional, FHA and VA are all accepted, which suggests the condition would pass an FHA/VA appraisal — the opposite signal from an as-is listing.

quality.text: Real money has already gone into this one: Wolf and Thermador appliances, solid cherry custom cabinets, finished basement, professional landscaping. And carrying costs are genuinely low — $40/mo HOA, $2,083/yr tax.

competition.text: 5,825 views and 593 saves in 27 days. A lot of eyes on it, so don't expect a deep discount to land uncontested.

monthly.note: Assumes 20% down ($479,920 loan) at 6.5% over 30 years — confirm with a lender. THE INSURANCE LINE IS THE BIG UNKNOWN and is an estimate, not a quote. Rockrimmon is named as a wildfire-risk area: if it prices as interface property, expect $375-710/mo instead of $450, and the worst case cited in the videos is $15,000/yr, which would be $1,250/mo. That single line can swing the payment by $800. Zillow shows $3,719/mo, but its insurance figure is generic.

offer.rationale: The county's own actual value is $580,069, it's already been cut once from $620,000, and it hasn't sold in 27 days during what's still decent season. Citywide, the average home sold $79k below the average list price. Most importantly you need to buy below ask here to preserve a reserve — a 1978 house with an undisclosed roof at the very top of budget is exactly the trap of buying something that only works if nothing goes wrong. Counterweight: 593 saves means real competition, so this is a serious offer rather than a lowball.
asks: A Class 4 impact-resistant roof, specified as such — highest-value single ask, saves 20-30% on premium every year [T04]
Proof of insurability: a binder or written quote before the inspection deadline, given Rockrimmon's wildfire pricing [T04]
Enough inspection days for a structural engineer AND a sewer scope, not just a general inspection [T04]
Seller concessions toward closing costs, commonly $8,000-10,000 in this market [T05]
A rate buydown rather than a further price cut if they resist — often saves more per month [T05]
